input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: Argument.get_help_record returns self.help unchanged, so the second element of the tuple is None for an undocumented argument even though format_arguments now feeds every record straight into formatter.write_dl without a fallback.
- failure path: A command declares two arguments and sets help on only one; running it with --help makes write_dl measure and wrap a None description and the help command crashes with a TypeError instead of printing usage.

Reviewer finding
- description: Argument.get_help_record now returns (metavar, self.help) unconditionally. The return annotation is tuple[str, str], but self.help is None when no help was set. The old code substituted an empty string for those arguments.
- rationale: Trigger: a command where at least one Argument has help and another has no help. The None description is passed to formatter.write_dl at line 1323. HelpFormatter.write_dl wraps the description text, which likely fails on None (for example in wrap_text or a truthiness/len path), so --help can crash with a TypeError or print wrong output. The removed fallback `or (arg.make_metavar(ctx), "")` handled this case.
critique: The finding identifies Argument.get_help_record returning self.help unchanged (None for an undocumented argument). It says this None goes into formatter.write_dl without the removed empty-string fallback, which causes a TypeError on --help when one argument has help and another does not. That is the same mechanism and trigger as the label.
